title: "dicer stats"
description: "Show what instances use of the host, live"
---

Shows each running or paused instance's CPU, memory, network and disk use,
read on the host from its hypervisor process: nothing in the guest is asked.
Without names, every running or paused instance is shown, as they come and
go.

CPUPerc is a share of one host CPU, so 200% is two kept busy; the threads
emulating its devices count too. MemUsage is the hypervisor's resident host
memory / the guest memory committed to the instance, and MemPerc the one as
a share of the other. NetIO is what the guest received / transmitted, and
BlockIO what the hypervisor read / wrote: the guest's disks, and its own
files, such as the serial console log and a snapshot's memory. Reads served
from the host's page cache are not counted. Both are totals since the
instance started.

The column names are also the fields of a `--format` template, and the keys of
`--format` json.

The view is redrawn every second until Ctrl+C. With `--no-stream` it is shown
once, a second after asking, since CPU use is measured over that second.

## Usage

```console
$ dicer stats [NAME...] [flags]
```

## Examples

```console
$ dicer stats
$ dicer stats web db
$ dicer stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}}\t{{.CPUPerc}}\t{{.MemUsage}}'
$ dicer stats --no-stream --format json
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c`, `--columns strings` | Columns to display, comma-separated and in any case (default: all). |
| `--format string` | Output format: table, json, yaml, or a Go template, e.g. '{{.Name}}\t{{.State}}'. Default: `table`. |
| `--no-stream` | Show the stats once rather than live. |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only display names, one a line. |

## Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-D`, `--debug` | Trace every call to the daemon on stderr (or set `$DICER_DEBUG`). |
| `-r`, `--remote string` | Daemon to talk to: a remote's name, or an address (unix:///PATH or HOST:PORT) (default `$DICER_REMOTE`, then the current remote, then local). |
| `--timeout duration` | Give up on a call to the daemon after this long, e.g. 30s (0: never; streams such as logs -f and exec are not bounded). |
